openItems.explanation: Northgate Savings Bank sent no 2025 Form 1098 for the loan paid off in the June 20 refinance. The draft deducts $14,212.50 of January to June interest from the payoff and monthly statements on Schedule A line 8a. A person obtains the Form 1098 (or the lender's online copy) and confirms the amount; the debt itself qualifies: $598,400.00 refinanced with no cash out, under $750,000.

The clients' log shows four 2025 estimated payments, $8,000.00; their IRS account credits three, $6,000.00, and shows the January 15, 2026 payment (DP 2026-0115-68203) under tax year 2026. The draft claims $6,000.00 on line 26. A person asks the IRS to move it to 2025 (or the clients confirm it was meant for 2026); if moved, the refund rises from $4,669.02 to $6,669.02. No penalty either way.

The September 22, 2025 gift of $2,500.00 to Anytown Children's Hospital Foundation has no contemporaneous written acknowledgment yet, so the draft leaves it out of Schedule A line 11. With the letter in hand before filing, line 11 rises by $2,500.00 and the tax falls by about $550.00 at the 22% rate.

Unsigned draft. The return is due April 15, 2026; both spouses sign. Additional Medicare Tax of $162.00 was not withheld and is paid with the return; a Form W-4 change avoids it next year. The $30,000.00 HANGS bonus paid January 9, 2026 belongs on the 2026 return. Resolve MORT-01, EST-01 and CHAR-01 first; nothing has been filed. Washington has no state income tax return.

rules.question: What is the 2025 standard deduction for a joint return?
rules.whyItMatters: Itemizing helps only if Schedule A is larger than the standard deduction.
rules.excerpt: For 2025, the standard deduction amount has been increased for all filers. The amounts are: ... $31,500-Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse.
matchPhrases: for 2025, the standard deduction amount has been increased for all filers
$31,500-married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
rules.ruleOrLimit: Standard deduction $31,500 for married filing jointly.
rules.hangsApplication: Itemized deductions of $55,746.50 are larger than $31,500.00, so line 12e uses Schedule A.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: How is the tax figured on taxable income of $100,000 or more for a joint return?
rules.whyItMatters: The Tax Table stops at $100,000; above it the Tax Computation Worksheet gives the tax as a rate times income less a subtraction amount.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet, Section B.
rules.excerpt: Section B-Use if your filing status is Married filing jointly or Qualifying surviving spouse ... At least $100,000 but not over $206,700 x 22% (0.22) ... $10,172.00 ... Over $206,700 but not over $394,600 x 24% (0.24) ... $14,306.00
matchPhrases: section b-use if your filing status is married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
rules.ruleOrLimit: Joint return: 22% less $10,172.00 up to $206,700; 24% less $14,306.00 up to $394,600; higher rows likewise.
rules.hangsApplication: The ordinary part of taxable income, $178,893.86, is in the 22% row: $29,184.65. The whole $214,893.86 would be $37,268.53 in the 24% row.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: At what rates are qualified dividends taxed on a 2025 joint return?
rules.whyItMatters: Qualified dividends are taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% by where taxable income falls, through the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet-Line 16, lines 6 and 13.
rules.excerpt: Enter: $48,350 if single or married filing separately, $96,700 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse ... Enter: $533,400 if single, $300,000 if married filing separately, $600,050 if married filing jointly ... Multiply line 17 by 15% (0.15).
matchPhrases: $96,700 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
$600,050 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
multiply line 17 by 15% (0.15)
rules.pageOrSection: Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, lines 6, 13 and 18
rules.ruleOrLimit: 0% up to $96,700 of taxable income, 15% up to $600,050, 20% above, for a joint return.
rules.hangsApplication: The $36,000.00 HANGS dividend is all qualified. The ordinary income below it, $178,893.86, already passes $96,700, so none is at 0%; all $36,000.00 is at 15%, $5,400.00.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: Is the HANGS dividend a qualified dividend?
rules.whyItMatters: Box 1b of Form 1099-DIV is qualified only if the stock was held more than 60 days around the ex-dividend date.
rules.excerpt: Dividends you received on any share of stock that you held for less than 61 days during the 121-day period that began 60 days before the ex-dividend date.
matchPhrases: dividends you received on any share of stock that you held for less than 61 days during the 121-day period that began 60 days before the ex-dividend date
rules.ruleOrLimit: A dividend on stock held less than 61 days in the 121-day window is not qualified.
rules.hangsApplication: Celeste Whitford has held her 60% since the company began; the December 19, 2025 dividend from a domestic C corporation is qualified: line 3a $36,000.00.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: How much state and local tax can a joint return deduct for 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: The SALT deduction is capped; the 2025 cap is $40,000, reduced when modified AGI passes $500,000 but not below $10,000.
rules.effective: Instructions for Schedule A (2025), What's New and line 5e worksheet.
rules.excerpt: The overall limit on the deduction for state and local income, sales, and property taxes has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately). The overall limit is reduced if your modified adjusted gross income is more than $500,000 ... but will not be reduced below $10,000 ... Multiply line 6 by 30% (0.30).
matchPhrases: the overall limit on the deduction for state and local income, sales, and property taxes has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately)
the overall limit is reduced if your modified adjusted gross income is more than $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately) but will not be reduced below $10,000
multiply line 6 by 30% (0.30)
rules.pageOrSection: What's New; line 5e, State and Local Tax Deduction Worksheet
rules.ruleOrLimit: SALT limit $40,000, less 30% of modified AGI over $500,000, not below $10,000.
rules.hangsApplication: Modified AGI $270,640.36 is under $500,000, so the limit stays $40,000.00. Washington has no income tax; the real estate tax ($12,480.00) and general sales tax ($4,365.80), $16,845.80, are under the limit and deducted in full.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025), Itemized Deductions

rules.question: Can Washington residents deduct general sales tax, and how?
rules.whyItMatters: With no state income tax, the clients deduct general sales tax instead, from actual receipts or the optional tables.
rules.excerpt: If you elect to deduct state and local general sales taxes instead of income taxes, you must check the box on line 5a. To figure your state and local general sales tax deduction, you can use either your actual expenses or the optional sales tax tables.
matchPhrases: if you elect to deduct state and local general sales taxes instead of income taxes, you must check the box on line 5a
you can use either your actual expenses or the optional sales tax tables
rules.pageOrSection: Line 5a, State and local general sales taxes
rules.ruleOrLimit: General sales tax by actual receipts or the optional tables; box 5a checked.
rules.hangsApplication: The clients kept receipts and card statements: $4,365.80 at the general rate (no vehicle purchase). Line 5a uses actual expenses with the box checked; the optional table amount was not compared.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025), Itemized Deductions

rules.question: Is all of the mortgage interest deductible?
rules.whyItMatters: Interest on home acquisition debt taken out after December 15, 2017 is deductible on up to $750,000 of that debt.
rules.excerpt: For qualifying debt taken out after December 15, 2017, you can only deduct home mortgage interest on up to $750,000 ($375,000 if you are married filing separately) of that debt.
matchPhrases: for qualifying debt taken out after december 15, 2017, you can only deduct home mortgage interest on up to $750,000 ($375,000 if you are married filing separately) of that debt
rules.pageOrSection: Limit on loans taken out after December 15, 2017
rules.ruleOrLimit: $750,000 of home acquisition debt for loans after December 15, 2017.
rules.hangsApplication: The 2019 loan of $680,000.00 bought the main home; $598,400.00 was refinanced in June 2025 with no cash out. Every dollar is under $750,000, so all interest is deductible: $26,700.70.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025), Itemized Deductions

rules.question: Does the June refinance stay home acquisition debt?
rules.whyItMatters: A refinance is acquisition debt only up to the old principal just before the refinancing.
rules.excerpt: Any secured debt you use to refinance home acquisition debt is treated as home acquisition debt. However, the new debt will qualify as home acquisition debt only up to the amount of the balance of the old mortgage principal just before the refinancing.
matchPhrases: any secured debt you use to refinance home acquisition debt is treated as home acquisition debt
the new debt will qualify as home acquisition debt only up to the amount of the balance of the old mortgage principal just before the refinancing
rules.ruleOrLimit: Refinanced debt up to the old principal remains acquisition debt.
rules.hangsApplication: The new loan, $598,400.00 (Form 1098 box 2), equals the principal paid off ($598,400.00): no cash out, all acquisition debt.
rules.sourceTitle: Publication 936 (2025), Home Mortgage Interest Deduction

rules.question: What goes on line 8a when the old lender sent no Form 1098?
rules.whyItMatters: Line 8a is for interest reported on Form 1098; the old lender should have issued one for January to June.
rules.excerpt: Enter on line 8a mortgage interest and points reported to you on Form 1098 unless one or more of the limits on home mortgage interest apply to you.
matchPhrases: enter on line 8a mortgage interest and points reported to you on form 1098 unless one or more of the limits on home mortgage interest apply to you
rules.ruleOrLimit: Line 8a carries the interest reported on Forms 1098.
rules.hangsApplication: Pinecrest Home Loans reported $12,488.20. Northgate Savings Bank sent no Form 1098; the draft includes the $14,212.50 from its payoff and monthly statements on line 8a (MORT-01).
rules.unresolved: A person obtains the Northgate Savings Bank Form 1098 (or its online copy) and confirms the $14,212.50 before filing (MORT-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025), Itemized Deductions

rules.question: Which charitable gifts can be deducted?
rules.whyItMatters: A gift of $250 or more needs a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charity.
rules.effective: Instructions for Schedule A (2025), Gifts of $250 or more.
rules.excerpt: You can deduct a gift of $250 or more only if you have a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charitable organization.
matchPhrases: you can deduct a gift of $250 or more only if you have a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the charitable organization
rules.pageOrSection: Gifts to Charity, Gifts of $250 or more
rules.ruleOrLimit: No deduction for a $250-or-more gift without the written acknowledgment.
rules.hangsApplication: Five gifts have their acknowledgment or are under $250 ($12,200.00). The $2,500.00 to Anytown Children's Hospital Foundation has none yet and is left out (CHAR-01).
rules.unresolved: A person obtains the written acknowledgment before the return is filed; with it, line 11 rises by $2,500.00 (CHAR-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule A (Form 1040) (2025), Itemized Deductions

rules.question: Are the cash gifts within the AGI limit?
rules.whyItMatters: Cash gifts to public charities are limited to 60% of AGI.
rules.excerpt: Your deduction for the cash contributions is 60% of your AGI.
matchPhrases: your deduction for the cash contributions is 60% of your agi
rules.ruleOrLimit: Cash gifts to 50% limit organizations: up to 60% of AGI.
rules.hangsApplication: Gifts of $12,200.00 are 4.5% of AGI $270,640.36: far under 60%, no carryover.
rules.sourceTitle: Publication 526 (2025), Charitable Contributions

rules.question: Is Schedule B required?
rules.whyItMatters: Interest or ordinary dividends over $1,500 must be listed by payer on Schedule B.
rules.effective: Instructions for Schedule B (2025), General Instructions.
rules.excerpt: You had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends.
matchPhrases: you had over $1,500 of taxable interest or ordinary dividends
rules.ruleOrLimit: Schedule B when interest or ordinary dividends exceed $1,500.
rules.hangsApplication: Interest $2,140.36 (Cobalt Harbor Bank) and dividends $36,000.00 (HANGS) both pass $1,500: Schedule B lists both payers. No foreign accounts (organizer Q12).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025)

rules.question: How much is the 2025 child tax credit?
rules.whyItMatters: The credit per qualifying child rose for 2025, and each child needs a valid SSN.
rules.excerpt: For 2025, the maximum CTC has increased to $2,200 per qualifying child, of which $1,700 can be claimed for the ACTC.
matchPhrases: for 2025, the maximum ctc has increased to $2,200 per qualifying child, of which $1,700 can be claimed for the actc
rules.ruleOrLimit: $2,200 per qualifying child.
rules.hangsApplication: Ivy, 11 at the end of 2025, lived with them all year and has a valid SSN: $2,200.00 on line 19.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: Does income reduce the child tax credit?
rules.whyItMatters: The credit phases out above modified AGI of $400,000 on a joint return.
rules.excerpt: Your modified adjusted gross income (AGI) is more than the amount shown below for your filing status. Married filing jointly -$400,000.
matchPhrases: married filing jointly -$400,000
rules.ruleOrLimit: Phase-out above $400,000 of modified AGI, joint return.
rules.hangsApplication: Modified AGI $270,640.36 is under $400,000: no reduction.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Schedule 8812 (Form 1040) (2025)

rules.question: Do the Whitfords owe Additional Medicare Tax?
rules.whyItMatters: The 0.9% tax applies to combined Medicare wages over $250,000 on a joint return; each employer withholds it only over $200,000 of its own wages.
rules.excerpt: A 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies to your Medicare wages ... above a threshold amount ... Married filing jointly $250,000 ... Your employer is responsible for withholding the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on your Medicare wages ... paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.
matchPhrases: a 0.9% additional medicare tax applies to your medicare wages
married filing jointly $250,000
your employer is responsible for withholding the 0.9% additional medicare tax on your medicare wages or rrta compensation paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year
rules.ruleOrLimit: 0.9% of Medicare wages over $250,000 (joint).
rules.hangsApplication: Medicare wages $150,000.00 (HANGS) and $118,000.00 (school district), $268,000.00 together: $18,000.00 over, $162.00. Neither employer passed $200,000, so none was withheld; it is due with the return (Schedule 2 line 11).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 8959 (2025), Additional Medicare Tax

rules.question: Do the Whitfords owe the net investment income tax?
rules.whyItMatters: The 3.8% tax applies to the smaller of net investment income or modified AGI over $250,000 (joint).
rules.excerpt: Individuals who have for the tax year (a) MAGI that's over an applicable threshold amount, and (b) NII, must pay 3.8% of the smaller of (a) or (b) as their NIIT ... Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse is $250,000.
matchPhrases: must pay 3.8% of the smaller of (a) or (b) as their niit
married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse is $250,000
rules.ruleOrLimit: 3.8% of the smaller of NII or MAGI over $250,000.
rules.hangsApplication: Net investment income $38,140.36 (interest $2,140.36, dividends $36,000.00); MAGI $270,640.36 is $20,640.36 over: 3.8% of $20,640.36 is $784.33 (Schedule 2 line 12). A dividend from a C corporation is investment income even though she works there.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 8960 (2025), Net Investment Income Tax

rules.question: Is any alternative minimum tax due?
rules.whyItMatters: The SALT deduction is added back for AMT; the 2025 exemption for a joint return is $137,000.
rules.excerpt: The exemption amount on Form 6251, line 5, has increased to $88,100 ($137,000 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse ...). For 2025 ... the 26% tax rate applies to the first $239,100.
matchPhrases: the exemption amount on form 6251, line 5, has increased to $88,100 ($137,000 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
the 26% tax rate applies to the first $239,100
rules.ruleOrLimit: Exemption $137,000 (joint); 26% on the first $239,100 of the excess.
rules.hangsApplication: AMT income is taxable income plus the SALT deduction; less the $137,000 exemption, the tentative minimum tax is well below the regular tax: no AMT.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 6251 (2025), Alternative Minimum Tax

rules.question: Is there an underpayment penalty?
rules.whyItMatters: Withholding and timely estimates must reach the smaller of 90% of the 2025 tax or 110% of the 2024 tax when 2024 AGI was over $150,000.
rules.excerpt: If your adjusted gross income (AGI) for 2024 was more than $150,000 ($75,000 if your 2025 filing status is married filing separately), substitute 110% for 100% in (2) above.
matchPhrases: if your adjusted gross income (agi) for 2024 was more than $150,000 ($75,000 if your 2025 filing status is married filing separately), substitute 110% for 100% in (2) above
rules.pageOrSection: Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty
rules.ruleOrLimit: Required payment: smaller of 90% of 2025 tax or 110% of 2024 tax (2024 AGI over $150,000).
rules.hangsApplication: 2024 AGI was $251,880.00, so 110% of the 2024 tax is $32,340.00; 90% of the 2025 tax is $29,997.88, the smaller. Withholding alone, $32,000.00, treated as paid evenly, covers every installment: no penalty, no Form 2210.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 2210 (2025), Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals

rules.question: Which estimated payments go on line 26?
rules.whyItMatters: Line 26 is the estimated tax actually paid for 2025.
rules.excerpt: Enter any estimated federal income tax payments you made for 2025.
matchPhrases: enter any estimated federal income tax payments you made for 2025
rules.ruleOrLimit: Line 26: the 2025 estimated payments.
rules.hangsApplication: The clients paid four installments, $8,000.00. Their IRS account credits three, $6,000.00, to 2025; the January 15, 2026 payment shows under 2026. The draft claims $6,000.00 (EST-01).
hangsFactsUsed: Estimated payments log and IRS account
rules.unresolved: A person asks the IRS to move the January 15, 2026 payment to 2025 (or the clients confirm it was meant for 2026); if moved, line 26 is $8,000.00 and the refund rises by $2,000.00 (EST-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025)

rules.question: Which 2025 Form 1040 lines does the draft fill?
rules.whyItMatters: The 2025 form splits adjusted gross income into lines 11a and 11b and adds line 13b for Schedule 1-A.
rules.excerpt: 11a Subtract line 10 from line 9. This is your adjusted gross income ... 13b Additional deductions from Schedule 1-A, line 38 ... 26 2025 estimated tax payments and amount applied from 2024 return
matchPhrases: subtract line 10 from line 9. this is your adjusted gross income
additional deductions from schedule 1-a, line 38
2025 estimated tax payments and amount applied from 2024 return
rules.ruleOrLimit: Lines 1a to 37 of the 2025 form.
rules.hangsApplication: The draft fills lines 1a, 1z, 2b, 3a, 3b, 9, 10, 11a, 11b, 12e, 13a, 13b, 14 to 26, 33 and 34; Schedule 1-A has no entries (no tips, overtime, car loan interest or senior deduction).
rules.sourceTitle: Form 1040 (2025), U.S. Individual Income Tax Return

excluded.why: Washington has no personal income tax; there is no state return to prepare.
No qualified tips, overtime premium or new-vehicle loan interest, and neither spouse is 65 or older.

changes.note: P.L. 119-21 raised the 2025 limit to $40,000 for a joint return, reduced above $500,000 of modified AGI.

changes.topic: Standard deduction and child tax credit
changes.note: P.L. 119-21 set the 2025 standard deduction at $31,500 (joint) and the child tax credit at $2,200.
